planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil once nights stay reliably above 55F.

directions: Gogosari is a Romanian heirloom 'cheese pepper' prized for its flattened, tomato-shaped fruit with thick, crisp walls that ripen from green to deep burgundy-red. It has been grown commercially in central and eastern Romania for roughly a century and remains a key ingredient in zacusca, the traditional Romanian roasted vegetable spread. The blocky, ribbed fruit is well suited to roasting and pickling whole, since its flattened shape and thick flesh make for easy peeling after charring. Give plants full sun and even moisture, and stake heavily fruiting plants since the dense, fleshy peppers can weigh down branches.
sources: Slow Food Foundation Ark of Taste

common_name: Carmagnola Pepper (Peperone di Carmagnola, Piedmontese IGP Sweet Pepper)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant after danger of frost has passed, in well-drained, sandy loam soil.

directions: Carmagnola pepper is a Piedmontese landrace grown for over a century around the town of Carmagnola near Turin, where it carries Italian IGP protected status and is cultivated in several traditional fruit shapes including blocky square, elongated horn, and flattened tomato-like forms. Fruit matures from green through yellow to red with notably thick, sweet, easily peeled flesh once roasted. It is traditionally eaten raw with bagna cauda, roasted and peeled, or preserved in oil or vinegar. Grow in full sun on sandy, well-drained soil and harvest by hand as fruit colors fully for best sweetness.
sources: Consorzio di Tutela del Peperone di Carmagnola IGP

common_name: Red Belgian Pepper (Early Heirloom Sweet Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; this fast-maturing heirloom suits short-season gardens where longer-season bells never fully ripen.

directions: Red Belgian is a compact, early heirloom sweet pepper valued by northern gardeners for its speed to harvest, with blocky conical fruit reaching edible creamy-yellow stage well before most bells and fully ripening to sweet, thick-walled red. Its naturally shorter season and productive, compact plants make it a reliable choice where summers are cool or short. Harvest some fruit at the yellow stage for a milder, crisper bite, or let fruit finish to red for full sweetness. Provide full sun and consistent moisture, and stake plants in windy sites since the compact branches can still be weighed down by heavy fruit set.
sources: Seed catalog descriptions (True Leaf Market, Tradewinds Fruit)

common_name: Yankee Bell Pepper (Open-Pollinated Northern-Adapted Bell Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Yankee Bell was selected for reliable performance and earlier maturity in cool northern growing regions.

directions: Yankee Bell is an open-pollinated blocky bell pepper selected specifically for the shorter, cooler growing seasons of northern gardens, producing uniform three- to four-lobed fruit on sturdy, well-branched plants. Fruit can be picked green at around 60 days from transplant or left to ripen fully red for sweeter flavor at roughly 80 days. Its stronger branching habit helps support fruit load without staking in most gardens. Grow in full sun with even moisture and side-dress with compost at first fruit set to sustain production through the season.
